name: rasa.module.notes
description: Portable notes and the decision ledger, one record per file: notebooks (directories), tags, pins, family-wide links and daily notes, plus the ratified decision ledger that turns a working note into a decision and a decision into canon. Built to the records-family/1 standard shared with rasa.module.schedule, rasa.module.crm and rasa.module.messages: a strict-YAML frontmatter grammar, JSON Schemas as the field law, an atomic CLI (.claude/bin/notes) that writes every change with an append-only history line, and a validator (.claude/bin/check-notes) that enforces every numbered invariant. The one thing that varies per project — where a decision becomes law — is delegated to the project-owned .claude/notes-canon.md seam and notes/notes.config.yml; `notes canonize` hard-stops until it is declared.

rasa.note: v0.2.0 EXTENDS the v0.1.x institutional-memory spine into a full notes module (owner decision 2026-09-28: 'extend module.notes' rather than a separate notebook module). Tier 1 of the working -> decision -> canon pipeline is now any note in any notebook; tier 2 is the decision ledger (notes/decisions/DEC-nnnn-*.md, frozen from ratification, superseded never edited, 'superseded' derived); tier 3 is the project's canon, named by config canon_target and recorded by `notes canonize` (which never writes canon itself). Built to the rasa.module.tasks v1.0.0 standard: numbered invariants (F-01..F-27 family, N-01..N-10 notes), JSON Schemas under .claude/schemas/notes/, one atomic CLI, an append-only notes/history.tsv, and a validator. records.py (the family core) is byte-identical across notes/schedule/crm/messages; bin/check-manifest proves it. Removed on the module.tasks v1.0.0 precedent: the vendored source clone bin/init used to drop into the consumer tree, the identity stamp, and the /sync /promote /whoami skills (which overwrote same-named parent skills under directory-mirror — and /promote collided with this module's own promotion verb). Boundary unchanged: this is human-authored, ordered, ratified markdown; similarity recall is the kernel's memory (rasa.module.ingest), a soft sibling. Cross-references into schedule/crm/messages/tasks are SOFT: resolved when mounted, unverifiable-but-legal when not, never requires.elements[].

identity.one_liner: the RasaOS module for notes and the decision ledger
identity.subject: notes, notebooks and ratified decisions
identity.goal: bring structured notes and a decision ledger into a project as an installable RasaOS module

element.description: Element-owned files mirrored into the install target per canon ELEMENT_CONTRACT.md §7. Refreshed on every Element upgrade, so nothing here holds project state. The seam, the config and the notes/ ledger are NOT here — they are project-owned (see seed.files).

files.note: The law: the records-family/1 conventions (identical in all four family modules) followed by the notes law — notebooks, notes, the decision ledger, the three-tier pipeline, the canon seam, the kernel-memory boundary. Every rule is marked with its invariant id or 'judgement'.
JSON Schemas (draft 2020-12 subset) for the note, the decision and notes.config.yml. Both the interop artifact and the enforced field law: records.py evaluates them.
The two notes skills — /note and /decide. Only names inside this module's vocabulary: directory-mirror overwrites same-named skills silently.

The two programs (notes, check-notes) and their package rasa_notes/ (records.py family core, model, validate, cli, FAMILY). Pure standard library; no network, no version control. Overlays .claude/bin/ without deleting other modules' programs.
What this module ships and where each file lands. Author-time; not installed.
The design record: why notes was extended, the records-family/1 design, the invariant map. Author-time; not installed.

seed.description: One-time, project-owned files copied at install only (skip-if-exists / init-only-with-sha), per canon ELEMENT_CONTRACT.md §7. They belong to the project the moment they land and are never overwritten by an Element upgrade.

files.note: The judgement half of the seam: what canon is here, the promotion criteria, any hard gate. The machine half (canon_target, categories) is in notes/notes.config.yml.
What the project declares: default and journal notebooks, the notebook/type/tag/category vocabularies (declare to constrain), canon_target (the hard-stop), actors, default_actor.
The append-only history log, header row only. Written by the notes tool, never by hand.
The default notebook (bin/init does not implement scaffold.directories, so directories ship as placeholders).
The decision ledger directory (reserved; decisions live only here).
Stamped with the Element HEAD SHA at init; written only when absent. When co-installed under a parent that stamps its own lockfile, the parent's is authoritative (single-writer-per-path, Lock L-004).

scaffold.description: bin/init does not implement scaffold.directories; the notes/ directories ship as seed .keep placeholders instead, so this stays empty rather than declaring something nothing performs.
